title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Replace combinational 32-bit divider with a 1-bit/cycle iterative DIV/REM FSM that stalls EX, and merge the three multipliers into one 33x33 signed product
motivation:
The baseline Fmax is 5.442 MHz. The worst path is 199.8 ns / 150 logic
levels: MEM/WB.rd -> forward_unit -> EX operand mux -> u_alu -> the EX/MEM
alu_result register (absorbed into the dmem BSRAM address register). The only thing
in alu.sv that deep is the purely combinational `/` and `%` (four 32-bit
array dividers, DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU, each ~32 cascaded 32-bit subtract/mux
rows). It also accounts for most of the 12.3k LUT4 (target 10k).
CoreMark's timed region runs almost no divides: list/matrix/state/CRC
kernels use add/sub/shift/mul, and the divides are in portme/timing code
outside the start/stop markers. So a slow divider costs next to no
iterations/cycle, while a combinational one caps the whole core's clock.
Fitness = iter/cycle x Fmax, and iter/cycle is already good
(~2.23 CoreMark/MHz), so Fmax is the lever that matters.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Remove the combinational divide/remainder from the EX critical path and do it
over many cycles instead:

1. Iterative divider (inside alu.sv, so test_alu.py's source list is unchanged):
   a radix-2 restoring shift-subtract unit with regs {rem[32:0], quo[31:0],
   divisor[31:0], cnt[5:0], busy, done, neg_q, neg_r, special-case flags}.
   On start it latches |a|, |b| (sign-magnitude for DIV/REM) and resolves
   the RV32M special cases right away (div-by-0 -> quo=all-ones, rem=a;
   INT_MIN/-1 -> quo=INT_MIN, rem=0). Those cases finish in 1 cycle; the
   rest take 32 iterations plus 1 fix-up cycle that conditionally negates
   the quotient or remainder. Each iteration is one 33-bit subtract and a mux,
   about 10-12 levels, far from critical. Ports added to alu: clock, reset,
   div_start (EX holds a valid DIV* op, the result is not ready yet, and there is no
   dmem stall), div_busy, and div_done/result-valid. The `out` path for all
   non-div ops stays combinational.

2. Pipeline integration (ex_stage.sv, hazard_unit.sv, core.sv): while EX
   holds a DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU whose result is not ready, raise div_stall.
   It holds the PC (stall_if), holds ID/EX (stall_id=1, flush_id=0,
   redirect cannot fire because a DIV never redirects), and makes EX/MEM
   capture a bubble (valid=0, reg_write=0, mem_read/mem_write=0) so
   MEM and WB drain normally. Operand-capture subtlety: while the DIV sits in
   EX, older producers leave EX/MEM and MEM/WB, so the forwarded rs1/rs2
   values disappear. The divider therefore latches the post-forward rs1/rs2
   on the start cycle and uses them for the arithmetic. It keeps the raw
   latched values for EX/MEM.rs1_val/rs2_val so RVFI rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata
   stay correct. A done flag keeps the result until EX/MEM actually
   advances (a dmem stall can delay that), then clears. dmem_stall keeps
   priority over div_stall for the EX/MEM hold. Tie-break rule: if dmem_stall
   is active, EX/MEM holds; otherwise, if div_stall is active, EX/MEM
   takes a bubble.

3. ALTOPS consistency: under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the result is
   still the (a +/- b) ^ const stand-in, computed from the latched operands.
   The same busy/done handshake runs with a shortened count (1 extra
   cycle), so formal still exercises the div stall, operand latching and
   bubble logic within the depth-20 BMC and the liveness check.

4. Multiplier merge (alu.sv): replace the three 64-bit products (mul_ss,
   mul_uu, mul_su) with one signed 33x33 product
   $signed({a[31]&a_signed, a}) * $signed({b[31]&b_signed, b}), where
   a_signed = MULH|MULHSU and b_signed = MULH. MUL takes p[31:0] and the
   MULH* ops take p[63:32]. That is one DSP cascade instead of three, one
   fewer wide output mux level on the ALU path, and fewer DSP/LUT
   resources for placement.

Expected result: with the divider gone, the critical path becomes
forwarding -> ALU (DSP multiplier or the 32-bit compare/adder) -> EX/MEM,
or the branch-resolve -> redirect -> PC path, roughly 20-40 levels on
GW2A. Fmax should go from 5.4 MHz to ~30-50 MHz (5-9x) with CoreMark
iter/cycle essentially unchanged (<0.5% loss from the rare in-region
divides). LUT4 should drop by several thousand. The real gain is far beyond
the schema's +50% cap.

changes.description: Add clock/reset/div_start inputs and div_busy/div_done outputs. Replace the combinational `/` and `%` with a radix-2 restoring iterative divider that latches operands on start, handles div-by-0 and INT_MIN/-1 in 1 cycle, and negates the result in a final fix-up cycle. Keep the ALTOPS branch with the (a+/-b)^const results through the same handshake, using a short count. Collapse mul_ss/mul_uu/mul_su into a single 33x33 signed multiply selected by op.

Decode is_div (alu_op in DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU) and drive div_start when a valid div op is in EX, its result is not done and there is no dmem stall. Export div_stall to the hazard unit. While div_stall && !stall, load a bubble into EX/MEM (valid=0, ctrl reg_write/mem_read/mem_write cleared). When the DIV finally advances, write the divider's latched rs1/rs2 into EX/MEM rs1_val/rs2_val/write_data for RVFI. Clear the done flag when EX/MEM captures the result.

Add a div_stall input. Include it in stall_if and stall_id (hold, not bubble). Do not include it in flush_id. Leave stall_ex_mem/hold_mem_wb as dmem_stall only; the div bubble into EX/MEM is inserted inside ex_stage. Make sure load_use_hazard is re-evaluated only once ID/EX advances (an ID/EX hold from div_stall wins over the load-use bubble, as dmem_stall already does).
Wire div_stall from u_ex to u_hazard. No top-level IO change.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r1s0 (improvement, +784.41%): The combinational `/` and `%` in alu.sv (four 32-bit array dividers, ~150 logic levels) capped the core at 5.4 MHz, and CoreMark's timed region has almost no divides, so a 1-bit/cycle iterative DIV/REM FSM that stalls EX (latching post-forward operands on start, since forwarding sources drain while it waits) gives a large Fmax gain at negligible iter/cycle cost; first check the critical path for rarely-executed ops before tuning anything else.

title: Move MUL/DIV out of the 1-cycle EX ALU into a multi-cycle stalling M-unit (DSP multiplier + radix-2 iterative divider)
motivation:
The baseline's Fmax is 5.44 MHz (worst path 199.8 ns, 156 cells:
u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex). The EX-stage ALU computes three
64-bit products AND a fully combinational 32-bit signed/unsigned
divide + remainder every cycle, all behind the forwarding muxes. A
combinational 32/32 array divider is a ~32-deep chain of 32-bit
subtract/select rows — on GW2A LUT4 fabric that is ~200 ns and it is
also what drives the LUT count to 12.3k (target 10k). Every other
path in this 5-stage pipe (fwd mux -> 32b adder/compare -> redirect ->
PC mux) is on the order of 15-25 ns. So the whole core runs ~10x
slower than it needs to because of an operation that CoreMark almost
never executes in its timed region (at -O3 divisions by constants are
strength-reduced to MULH/shift; the hot code is list walking, state
machine switch, CRC, and matrix MUL/add). No prior experiments exist
on this core besides the baseline retest, so this is the first-order
structural bottleneck to remove.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the M-extension out of the combinational ALU into a separate
multi-cycle execution unit `rtl/muldiv.sv` that lives in EX and
stalls the front of the pipeline while busy:

1. alu.sv keeps only the RV32I ops (ADD/SUB/logic/SLT/shift/LUI). The
   `*`, `/`, `%` operators disappear from the single-cycle path. (The
   ALU_MUL..ALU_REMU encodings stay in core_pkg.sv; the decoder is
   unchanged, alu.sv returns 0 / don't-care for them.)

2. muldiv.sv (new):
   - Start: when a valid M-op sits in ID/EX and the unit is idle, latch
     the *post-forwarding* rs1/rs2 values (the same `rs1`/`rs2` wires
     the ALU/branch logic use in ex_stage) plus the op into internal
     registers. Operands are captured once, so later forwarding-source
     changes while EX is held are irrelevant.
   - Multiply: one 33x33 signed multiply on the *registered* operands
     (sign-extend a for MULH/MULHSU, b for MULH; zero-extend otherwise),
     product registered (lets Gowin map it to the DSP MULT36X36 /
     MULT18X18 blocks with input+output regs). Result = prod[31:0] for
     MUL, prod[63:32] otherwise. Latency: 3 cycles in EX (2 stall
     cycles). If `make timing` shows the DSP is far off the critical
     path, the implementer may collapse to 2 cycles (multiply directly
     from the latched operands into the EX/MEM capture) — but the
     default is the fully registered version so it can never become the
     new worst path.
   - Divide: radix-2 restoring divider on absolute values, 32
     iterations (one 33-bit subtract + shift per cycle), sign fix-up in
     the final cycle. Divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 are detected at
     start from the latched operands and complete immediately with the
     RV32M-defined results (DIV/DIVU by 0 -> all-ones, REM/REMU by 0 ->
     dividend, DIV INT_MIN/-1 -> INT_MIN, REM INT_MIN/-1 -> 0).
   - Outputs: `busy` (M-op in EX and result not yet ready) and
     `result`. Returns to idle when the EX/MEM register actually
     captures the result (i.e. done && !stall_ex_mem), so a coincident
     dmem stall cannot drop or double-issue the op.
   - `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS`: compute the same ALTOPS stand-ins as
     the current alu.sv ((a+b)^const / (a-b)^const) from the latched
     operands. Keep a short fixed latency (e.g. the multiply latency
     for all 8 ops) so formal exercises the stall path within the
     20-step BMC depth; the real divider's 33+ cycle latency must NOT
     be used under ALTOPS.

3. Pipeline integration (hazard_unit.sv / ex_stage.sv / core.sv):
   new input `ex_busy` to hazard_unit.
     stall_if |= ex_busy                (PC holds)
     stall_id |= ex_busy                (ID/EX holds the M-op; not flushed)
     flush_id stays (load_use||redirect)&&!dmem_stall — a load-use
       bubble must not overwrite the held M-op, so gate the load-use
       flush with !ex_busy as well (flush_id = (load_use && !ex_busy
       || redirect) && !dmem_stall; redirect cannot coincide with an
       M-op in EX since M-ops never redirect).
   ex_stage: while `ex_busy && !stall`, the EX/MEM register captures a
   bubble (valid=0, ctrl.reg_write=0, mem_read=mem_write=0) so the
   older instructions keep draining through MEM/WB and forwarding
   stays correct. On the completion cycle it captures the muldiv
   result as alu_result with the M-op's valid/ctrl/RVFI fields
   (rs1_val/rs2_val must be the latched operands, which equal the
   post-forward values RVFI expects). dmem stall keeps its existing
   precedence (EX/MEM hold).

Expected effect: the critical path collapses from ~200 ns to the
ordinary fwd-mux -> 32-bit add/compare -> redirect -> PC path
(~15-25 ns on GW2A-18, i.e. ~40-65 MHz, ~8-12x Fmax). LUT count drops
by several thousand (the array divider and three LUT multipliers are
gone; the DSP multiplier + ~150-LUT iterative divider replace them).
IPC cost: +2 cycles per MUL/MULH and ~+33 per DIV/REM. CoreMark's
timed region is dominated by non-M instructions; MULs are a few % of
dynamic instructions (matrix_mul_*), divides are ~0 in the timed loop,
so IPC should drop <10%. Net fitness: ~12 -> 80-130 iter/s. The +50%
below is the schema cap, not the estimate.

Correctness guards: riscv-formal (ALTOPS) proves the stall / operand
routing / RVFI discipline; test_alu.py's M-ext vectors are moved to a
new cocotb test driving muldiv.sv (start pulse, wait for done, compare)
so the exact-bit RV32M checks (div-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1, MULHSU sign
cases) keep running; cosim diffs every retired MUL/DIV against the ISS.

ALTOPS branch computes the riscv-formal stand-in formulas with short fixed latency.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r1s1 (regression, +736.39%): Also moving MUL into a 3-cycle stalling DSP unit, on top of r1s0's iterative divider, scored 101.37 vs r1s0's 107.19, most likely because the single-cycle 33x33 DSP multiply was already off r1s0's worst path (26.8 ns rf->ID->EX->hazard->PC), so the 2 extra stall cycles per MUL in CoreMark's matrix kernels cost iter/cycle with no Fmax to win back; only make an op multi-cycle when timing shows it is on the worst path.

title: IF-stage 64-entry BTB + 2-bit counters: zero-bubble taken branches/jumps, EX verifies every predicted next-PC
motivation:
IF and decode share one cycle (IF/ID is combinational), so every taken
branch, JAL and JALR resolves in EX and kills exactly one wrong-path
fetch slot (pc+4). Measured on the ISS over the timed CoreMark region
(2.92M instructions, 10 iterations, -O3, 2K): 529.6k conditional
branches (294.4k taken), 49.4k JAL, 13.7k JALR -> 12.24% of retired
instructions are taken control transfers = 0.122 cycles/instr of pure
redirect penalty. Baseline CPI is ~1.54 (12.12 iter/s / 5.442 MHz =
~449k cycles per 292k-instruction iteration), so perfect prediction is
worth ~8%. Fmax (5.4 MHz, 200 ns) is set entirely by the combinational
divider in EX; a front-end predictor hanging off the registered PC is
nowhere near that path, so the IPC gain passes straight into fitness.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a small direct-mapped branch target buffer read combinationally from
the registered IF PC, and carry the predicted next-PC down the pipeline
so EX can verify it.

Trace-driven sizing (same ISS run, allocate-on-taken, 2-bit counters,
1-cycle penalty per mispredict incl. predicted-taken-not-taken):
  entries  16: 80.8k mispred -> saves 0.095 CPI
  entries  32: 57.0k         -> saves 0.103 CPI
  entries  64: 51.5k         -> saves 0.105 CPI   <- chosen
  entries 128: 45.9k         -> saves 0.107 CPI
  64 + 4-deep RAS: 50.2k (+0.0004 CPI, not worth the logic; omit RAS)
64 entries removes ~86% of the redirect penalty: CPI ~1.54 -> ~1.43,
about +7.3% iter/cycle at unchanged Fmax.

BTB (new rtl/btb.sv): 64 entries, index pc[7:2], tag pc[19:8] (all
legal code lives below 0x00100000, so this tag is exact), stored
target[19:2], 2-bit saturating counter, is_jump bit, valid bit (valid
bits in resettable flops; tag/target/counter arrays have no reset so
Gowin may map them to LUT-RAM; flops are also acceptable at this size).
Prediction in IF: hit && (is_jump || ctr[1]) ->
next_pc = {pc[31:20], target, 2'b00}; otherwise pc+4. imem_addr stays
the registered PC, so the lookup is only on the PC-register D-input
path (a few LUT levels).

Update (1 cycle late, from the EX/MEM register so it adds nothing to EX
timing): for a valid branch/JAL/JALR in EX/MEM, on taken allocate or
refresh the entry (tag, target = pc_next, is_jump; counter = 2 on
allocate for branches, saturating increment on hit); on not-taken
decrement the counter only if hit (never allocate not-taken). A branch
never sits in EX/MEM for more than one cycle (dmem_stall requires a mem
op in EX/MEM), so each resolves and updates exactly once. Gate the
update with ex_mem.valid and !trap (misalign-faulted jumps must not
train).

Verification (the correctness guarantee, independent of BTB contents):
if_id_t and id_ex_t gain pred_npc [31:0]. EX computes the architectural
next PC exactly as today (misalign trap -> pc+4, jump -> jump_target,
taken branch -> branch_target, else pc+4) and sets
redirect = in.valid && (actual_npc != in.pred_npc), with
redirect_target = actual_npc. This covers predicted-taken-but-not-taken
(redirect to pc+4), wrong target (JALR/aliasing), and a stale or aliased
hit on a non-control instruction. Bubbles (valid=0, pc=0) must never
redirect. To keep the EX redirect cone shallow, precompute in ID
pred_taken = (pred_npc != pc+4) and pred_npc == pc+imm (both
forwarding-independent), so for branches EX only needs
branch_cond vs pred_taken; only JALR needs the post-forwarding
target compare. Existing priorities (redirect beats stall in IF;
ID/EX holds under dmem_stall with the redirect staying asserted
idempotently; load-use bubbles ID/EX while IF re-looks-up the same PC)
are unchanged. RVFI pc_wdata still comes from the actual next PC, so
formal/cosim contracts are untouched; a garbage BTB (symbolic formal
state, X-init) can only cost cycles, never correctness, and every
instruction still retires, so liveness holds.

Side benefit for later rounds: once another hypothesis removes the
combinational divider from the critical path, this structure lets
branch resolution move later (EX->MEM) cheaply, since correctly
predicted branches no longer pay the resolve latency.

changes.description: New module: 64-entry direct-mapped BTB (valid flops, tag pc[19:8], target[19:2], 2-bit counter, is_jump bit). Combinational lookup on IF pc -> pred_taken/pred_target; synchronous update port driven from EX/MEM (taken: allocate/refresh + counter up, counter=2 on branch allocate; not-taken hit: counter down; no allocate on not-taken).
Add pred_npc [31:0] to if_id_t and id_ex_t, plus pred_taken / pred_matches_pc_imm bits in id_ex_t precomputed in ID so the prediction travels with the instruction to EX.

Instantiate/consume BTB: next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target : (btb_taken ? btb_target : pc+4); emit out.pred_npc = the non-redirect next PC. Stall/flush/redirect priorities unchanged; imem_addr stays the registered pc.
Latch pred_npc into ID/EX with pred_taken = (pred_npc != pc+4) and pred_npc == pc+imm. Flush/reset clears them along with valid.

Replace redirect = taken||jump with redirect = in.valid && (actual_npc != in.pred_npc) (implemented via precomputed bits for branches/JAL, full compare only for JALR and non-control instructions predicted taken); redirect_target = actual_npc (existing pc_next expression incl. misalign -> pc+4). title: Cut EX redirect out of the IF-NOP-mux -> load-use -> stall chain and pre-register forwarding selects
motivation:
The champion's (r1s0) worst path is 26.8 ns / 48 cells / 21 levels:
u_rf (LUT-RAM, ID/EX rs1_val absorbed) -> u_ex (forward mux, 32-bit
branch compare -> redirect) -> u_if (out.instr = redirect ? NOP :
imem_data) -> u_hazard (load-use rs compare) -> stall_if/stall_id ->
PC reg (u_if/pc_18). r1s1's worst path is the same chain starting at
ID/EX.rs1_addr -> u_fwd compare. So the branch decision is serialised
with a second, independent decision (load-use) purely because the
hazard unit reads the redirect-masked IF/ID instruction. That masking
is logically redundant: load-use needs a LOAD in ID/EX while redirect
needs a branch/jump in ID/EX (decoder never sets mem_read together with
is_branch/is_jump), so they are never true in the same cycle; on
redirect flush_id already zeroes ID/EX and the PC takes
redirect_target with priority over stall.
Measured (make timing, place option 0, this worktree): all top-15 paths
are this chain, ending at PC CE or ID/EX rs*_val CE. Cell timeline:
RF LUT-RAM DO 7.6 ns -> bypass + 3 fwd-mux LUTs 11.9 -> 29-bit branch
compare carry chain 14.6 -> branch_cond/redirect 17.2 -> u_if NOP mux
(fanout 103) 18.6 -> rs1_addr 19.9 -> hazard rd==rs carry compare 21.8
-> u_id stall/flush 23.2 -> stall_id net (fanout 101) 24.4 -> PC CE
26.8 ns. i.e. 9.6 ns (36%) of the path is after redirect is known,
and only ~2 ns of it (redirect -> PC CE) is actually required.
Lesson r1s1: iter/cycle is
precious, so this is a pure-Fmax change with zero cycle-count impact.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Remove `redirect` from the IF->ID payload and from load-use detection,
and take the rd==rs comparators off the front of the EX path, without
changing any cycle-level behaviour (same stalls, bubbles, redirects ->
identical CoreMark cycle count; whole gain is Fmax).
  1. hazard_unit: load_use_hazard compares id_ex_rd against the RAW
     io_imemData[19:15] / [24:20] (wired in core.sv) instead of the
     NOP-muxed if_id instr; flush_if = !imem_ready only (redirect term
     dropped). Equivalence: load-use and redirect are mutually
     exclusive; during imem_stall a spurious load-use (garbage imem
     data) only turns "capture NOP bubble" into "flush-to-zero bubble"
     while the PC is already held; during dmem_stall flush_id is
     already gated off and stall_id is already 1.
  2. if_stage: out.instr = flush ? NOP : imem_data and out.valid =
     !flush with flush = imem stall only (redirect term dropped). ID/EX
     is cleared by flush_id(=redirect) so the wrong-path instruction
     never lands. Decoder/imm_gen now start at the imem register and
     imem_ready only, never at the EX compare.
  3. id_stage flush fanout trim: on flush clear only valid and the ctrl
     bits with architectural/side effects (reg_write, mem_read,
     mem_write, is_branch, is_jump, is_jalr, is_illegal); data fields
     (pc, rs*_val, imm, rd, rs*_addr, alu_op, ...) keep loading under
     !stall. Shrinks the redirect -> sync-reset net from ~150 flops to
     ~10 and frees the rs*_val flops for clean LUT-RAM output-register
     absorption. (is_div in ex_stage already gates on valid.)
  4. Registered forwarding selects: in ID compute, per operand, two
     match bits for the instruction being captured into ID/EX:
       m_ex  = id_ex.ctrl.reg_write && id_ex.rd != 0 && id_ex.rd == rs
               (producer will be in EX/MEM next cycle)
       m_mem = ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write && ex_mem.rd != 0 && ex_mem.rd == rs
               (producer will be in MEM/WB next cycle)
     using the raw imem rs fields, and register them in ID/EX (held
     with ID/EX on stall; flushed bubbles don't care). In EX:
       sel = (m_ex  && ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write) ? EX/MEM
           : (m_mem && mem_wb.ctrl.reg_write) ? MEM/WB : ID/EX value.
     The live reg_write AND keeps EX-misalign (JAL/JALR) and
     MEM-misalign (load) traps, which clear reg_write downstream, from
     forwarding. Valid because whenever ID/EX captures, EX/MEM and
     MEM/WB also advance (dmem_stall is in stall_id; div_stall holds
     ID/EX and the divider latches operands on its first EX cycle),
     and during dmem_stall EX/MEM is held and MEM/WB keeps its data, so
     the registered matches stay exact. This removes 2x(5-bit compare
     + priority) levels from the head of every EX path (branch compare,
     ALU -> dmem BSRAM address, JALR target).
     Fallback: if formal/cosim flag anything in step 4, drop it and
     keep steps 1-3, which are independently correct.
Expected: ~4-6 of 21 logic levels plus one ~150-fanout route removed
from the worst path; new worst path should be ID/EX -> fwd mux ->
compare/adder -> redirect -> PC or the ALU -> dmem address path.
Estimate +12-20% Fmax at unchanged iter/cycle.

title: Decouple fetch/decode from the EX redirect: raw-instruction decode, kill-bit-only ID/EX flush, registered pre-decoded forwarding selects
motivation:
The champion (r1s0, 48.1 MHz) is limited by one long combinational chain
that crosses four stage boundaries in a single cycle (26.8 ns, 48 cells,
modules u_rf/u_id -> u_ex -> u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id -> u_if; r1s1's
near-identical netlist shows the same chain starting at
u_id/reg_q.rs1_addr -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id and ending
at the ID/EX rs1_val register). The chain is:
ID/EX regs -> forward_unit 5-bit rd compares -> 3:1 forward mux -> 32-bit
branch compare / JALR misalign -> redirect -> if_stage's
`out.instr = (flush||redirect) ? NOP : imem_data` mux -> decoder, imm_gen,
regfile read address, hazard_unit load-use compare -> stall_if/stall_id/
flush_id -> PC enable and ID/EX enable/reset (hundreds of flops).
Everything after `redirect` is structurally redundant: when redirect
fires, flush_id already zeroes ID/EX and the PC mux already gives
redirect priority over stall, so the NOP substitution never changes
architectural state. The pipeline topology simply routes EX's resolution
through the fetch/decode payload instead of alongside it. The two
earlier Fmax hypotheses (r1s1 M-unit, r1s2 BTB) both kept this topology
and both stayed at or below 48 MHz, and lesson r1s2 says the BTB cannot
be re-applied until the redirect->PC path is re-timed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the pipeline control so that the fetch/decode stage never
depends combinationally on EX, and EX's operand selection never depends
on a same-cycle comparator:

1. Raw-instruction decode. if_stage drives `out.instr = imem_data` and
   `out.valid = imem_ready` with no redirect/flush mux. Decoder, imm_gen,
   regfile read addresses and the load-use compare all consume raw
   io_imemData (which in the timed wrapper is a flop output), so their
   depth starts at a register and ends at ID/EX. Wrong-path and
   imem-stall instructions are killed only via the ID/EX flush.

2. Kill-bit-only ID/EX flush. hazard_unit: flush_id =
   (redirect || load_use || !imem_ready) && !dmem_stall && !div_stall
   (imem-stall now bubbles through the flush; the div_stall gate keeps a
   waiting DIV from being killed by an imem stall). On flush, id_stage
   clears ONLY valid, ctrl.reg_write, ctrl.mem_read, ctrl.mem_write,
   ctrl.is_branch, ctrl.is_jump and the registered forward-select bits;
   every data field (pc, rs*_val, imm, rd, rs*_addr, alu_op, instr, ...)
   loads whenever the stage is not held. This cuts redirect's fanout
   from ~200 sync-reset flops to ~12, and keeps the data flops free of
   reset logic. Load-use on a raw wrong-path instruction during redirect
   is harmless: redirect already overrides the PC stall and the flush
   already overrides stall_id.

3. Registered, pre-decoded forwarding. In ID, compare the raw
   instruction's rs1/rs2 (instr[19:15], instr[24:20]) against ID/EX.rd
   (gated by ID/EX.ctrl.reg_write, rd != 0) -> fwd_ex bit, and against
   EX/MEM.rd (gated by EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write, rd != 0) -> fwd_wb bit,
   and store the four bits in ID/EX. This is exact because ID/EX only
   loads when EX/MEM also advances (stall_id covers every dmem_stall and
   div_stall), so the ID/EX occupant becomes the EX/MEM occupant and the
   EX/MEM occupant becomes MEM/WB, and a held ID/EX sees held EX/MEM and
   MEM/WB data. In EX, the forward mux becomes
   `fwd_ex_q && ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write ? ex_mem.alu_result :
    fwd_wb_q && mem_wb.ctrl.reg_write ? wb_w_data : in.rs*_val`, where the
   reg_write qualifiers are registered bits that absorb the late clears
   (EX misaligned-jump trap and MEM misaligned-load trap clear reg_write
   after the ID-time compare, and the div_stall bubble). forward_unit.sv
   is deleted or reduced to the ID-side compare. This removes the two
   LUT levels of 5-bit compare from every EX path: ALU -> EX/MEM,
   branch compare -> redirect -> PC, and the forward -> dmem address.

4. Cheap misalign in EX. The PC is always word-aligned (redirect is
   suppressed on misaligned targets), so branch/JAL target misalign is
   `imm[1]`, which is pre-decoded in ID into a registered bit; only JALR
   keeps a bit-1 sum (rs1[1] ^ imm[1] ^ (rs1[0] & imm[0])). redirect then
   depends on branch_cond plus a 2-input gate instead of the adders' low
   bits.

5. Dedicated AGU into the dmem address register. Measured probe
   (steps 1+2 only, Gowin place option 0): 52.36 MHz, and the
   redirect->hazard chain is gone. The new worst path is 24.4 ns,
   17 cells: u_id/reg_q.rs2_addr -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu ->
   dmem BSRAM address (the EX/MEM alu_result register is absorbed
   into the BSRAM address port). Step 3 removes the u_fwd part of this
   path. To also take the ALU result mux, shifter and multiplier off it,
   add an EX/MEM `mem_addr` field computed by a dedicated
   rs1_fwd + imm adder (loads/stores only) and drive io_dmemAddr,
   byte_mask, misalign and RVFI mem_addr from it. alu_result keeps
   the ALU/JAL value for writeback and forwarding.

After these changes the longest paths should be single-stage: ID/EX ->
forward mux -> ALU/branch compare -> EX/MEM or PC, and flop ->
decode/regfile -> ID/EX. That should land at 17-20 ns (about 50-58 MHz)
versus 26.8 ns, with iter/cycle unchanged (the stall/flush/forward
behaviour is cycle-for-cycle identical; only where decisions are
computed moves). Expected fitness about 120-135 vs 107.19.
Once implemented, run `make timing`. If the new worst path starts at the
regfile BSRAM (u_rf/regs_regs_*: the regfile is now 2 BSRAMs, bsram=6
in the log), add a Gowin `syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram"` attribute
(or equivalent) so the regfile read happens in ID from LUT-RAM and EX
starts from ordinary ID/EX flops rather than BSRAM clock-to-out. Keep
that change only if timing improves.

title: Fetch-stage bimodal BHT + predecoded pc+imm targets, so branch redirect can be registered (off the EX->hazard->PC critical path)
motivation:
Champion r1s0 runs at 48.1 MHz. Its worst path (26.8 ns, 21 levels) is
ID/EX rs1 -> forward mux -> 32-bit branch compare -> `redirect` -> IF
NOP-mux on the instruction -> hazard load-use compare -> stall_if/stall_id
-> PC and ID/EX register enables. r1s1's worst path (27.2 ns) is the same
chain. Every cycle the EX branch outcome has to reach the PC mux and the
ID/EX enables (~150 flops) combinationally, because a taken branch has to
redirect the very next fetch.
r1s2 showed that a BTB alone buys only IPC (+6-7%, 12.2% of CoreMark
instructions are taken branches/JAL/JALR, 1 bubble each). Its lesson
also says that on r1s0 a BTB lookup plus redirect compare would *lengthen* the
critical PC mux path. The predictor's real value here is different:
if most control transfers are predicted correctly at fetch, EX no longer
needs a same-cycle redirect. The mispredict can be registered and applied
a cycle later. That removes the whole EX->IF->hazard->PC/ID-enable chain
from timing, at the cost of a 2-cycle (instead of 1-cycle) penalty only
on the remaining mispredicts.
IF and decode share one cycle here (IF/ID is combinational). So the fetched
instruction's bits are available in the fetch cycle, and the target of a
JAL or conditional branch (pc + imm) can be computed at fetch with no BTB
target storage. Only branch *direction* needs to be predicted. In the timed
FPGA netlist io_imemData is an LFSR register, so the imem_data -> predecode
-> pc+imm adder -> PC path starts at a flop and is short (~10 ns).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. Fetch-stage prediction (if_stage.sv + new branch_predictor.sv):
   - Predecode imem_data in IF: is_jal (opcode 1101111), is_br
     (opcode 1100011, funct3 not 2/3), and the J-imm / B-imm (one 2:1 mux
     on opcode[3]). Compute pc_plus_imm = pc + imm.
   - BHT: 64 x 2-bit saturating counters indexed by pc[7:2], held in
     resettable flops (reset to 2'b01, weakly not-taken; resettable so
     Verilator/formal see no X). Combinational read from the registered PC.
   - pred_taken = fetch_valid && ((is_jal && !jimm[1]) ||
     (is_br && ctr[1] && !bimm[1])). Misaligned targets are never
     predicted, so EX's misalign trap path (pc+4) is never a
     predicted-taken case.
   - next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target : pred_taken ? pc_plus_imm :
     pc + 4. The existing priority is unchanged (redirect beats stall). With
     stall_if the PC holds, and the same instruction re-predicts next cycle.
   - if_id_t carries pred_taken and the 2-bit counter value that was read
     (both forced to 0 on flush/imem stall, like valid).
   - JALR is never predicted. It always takes the mispredict path
     (13.7k of 2.92M instructions; no RAS, too little benefit).
2. EX verification (ex_stage.sv): actual_taken = (branch_taken || is_jump)
   && !misalign_fault (today's `redirect` expression).
   mispredict = in.valid && (actual_taken != in.pred_taken). No 32-bit
   target compare is needed: a predicted-taken JAL/branch always
   predicts exactly pc+imm, which is its architectural target, and JALR is
   predicted not-taken. mispredict is *registered* into a new
   EX/MEM field. EX/MEM.pc_next already holds the correct architectural
   next PC (misalign -> pc+4, jump -> jump_target, taken -> branch_target,
   else pc+4). The combinational redirect/redirect_target outputs of
   ex_stage go away.
3. Late redirect (core.sv): redirect = ex_mem.valid && ex_mem.mispredict,
   redirect_target = ex_mem.pc_next. Both come straight from flops. It
   feeds the same consumers as today (if_stage PC load + IF NOP, hazard
   flush_if / flush_id). It is also a new `kill` input to ex_stage: on
   kill the wrong-path instruction currently in EX is written into EX/MEM
   as a bubble (valid=0, reg_write/mem_read/mem_write=0, mispredict=0),
   and is_div is gated with !kill so a wrong-path DIV never starts or
   stalls. The kill cycle is always dmem-stall free, because EX/MEM
   then holds the redirecting branch/jump, which is not a mem op. So
   EX/MEM always advances, redirect is exactly one cycle wide, and
   flush_id is not suppressed. The mispredict penalty is 2 cycles
   (IF/ID + ID/EX killed). Correctly predicted JAL/branches cost 0.
4. BHT training from the EX/MEM register (1 cycle late, all flop-sourced):
   when ex_mem.valid && ex_mem.ctrl.is_branch && !ex_mem.ctrl.is_illegal,
   write bht[ex_mem.pc[7:2]] <= sat_update(ex_mem.bht_ctr,
   ex_mem.branch_taken). The counter read at fetch travels
   IF -> ID/EX -> EX/MEM, so the BHT needs only one read port.
Correctness never depends on BHT contents. Every control instruction
is re-checked in EX, and RVFI pc_wdata still comes from pc_next. So
formal (pc_fwd/pc_bwd, liveness, unique) and cosim see the same
architectural stream. Only the two killed wrong-path slots are dropped.

Expected effect.
IPC, measured with an ISS trace of the timed CoreMark region (reference.py,
2.922M instructions: 529.6k conditional branches, 294.4k of them taken;
49.4k JAL; 13.7k JALR). Branch-direction mispredicts:
  BTFN static 111.2k | bimodal-64 51.8k | bimodal-128 54.5k | bimodal-256 44.3k
Today that is 357.5k redirect bubbles over ~4.49M cycles. With
bimodal-64: 0 for JAL, 2 x 13.7k for JALR and 2 x 51.8k for branches, about
131k bubbles. That saves ~226k cycles, ~5% fewer cycles (+5.3% iter/cycle).
BTFN (2 x 111k + 27k = 250k) would save only ~2.4%, so the BHT is worth its
~150 LUTs. 256 entries gains only another +0.4%, so keep 64.
Fmax: the EX-compare -> redirect -> IF NOP mux -> load-use -> stall ->
PC/ID-enable chain (the 26.8 ns worst path) disappears. What is left:
forward -> 32-bit compare -> XOR -> one flop (~13 ns); the forward ->
ALU/DSP-multiply -> EX/MEM (dmem BSRAM address) path; and the fetch
predecode -> 32-bit add -> PC mux path, which starts at a flop. I expect
Fmax of ~55-62 MHz (+15-28%), so fitness +20-30% overall.

title: Flatten EX: fully registered 2-bit forward selects, ID-premuxed operand B, one-hot registered ALU result and branch-op selects
motivation:
Measured on the champion (r2s1) with `make timing TARGET=bench`, place
option 0 = 72.8 MHz (median over options 67.6 MHz). All five worst paths
are ~19.0 ns arrival (13.7 ns data path) and all START at a forwarding
select qualifier, not at data:
  path 1 (12 cells): u_ex/reg_q.ctrl.reg_write (EX/MEM, fanout 81) ->
    rs1_31_s2 -> rs1_31_s0 (2-LUT forward mux) -> alu_a_31 (is_auipc
    operand mux) -> u_alu/mul_a_32 (sign-ext bit, a_signed decoded from
    the 5-bit op) -> DSP prod (3.76 ns) -> n764_s13/s9/s6/s3/s1/s0
    (SIX LUT levels of 19-way ALU result case + the is_jump ? pc+4 mux)
    -> EX/MEM alu_result.
  path 2 (11 cells): u_mem/reg_q.ctrl.mem_to_reg -> u_wb wb_w_data mux ->
    rs1 fwd mux -> alu_a -> adder -> result mux -> alu_result.
  paths 3-5 (11 cells): u_mem/reg_q.ctrl.mem_to_reg -> wb_w_data mux ->
    rs2 fwd mux -> n1038_s73/s34/s19/s12/s6/s2 (SIX LUT levels of branch
    compare + branch_op case) -> u_if/n37_s3 -> pc_w_28_s3 -> PC CE.
Of the ~11 LUT levels on each path, about 5 are select/decode logic whose
inputs are all known one cycle earlier in ID: the reg_write qualifiers,
the WB mem_to_reg mux, the AUIPC/alu_src operand mux, the multiplier
sign decode, the 5-bit ALU op decode, the is_jump link mux, and the
3-bit branch_op decode. Prior lessons show Fmax is what moves fitness
here (r2s1 gained +40% with identical cycles by shortening EX-starting
paths); this finishes that job inside EX without touching the pipeline
topology.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the pipeline topology, stall/flush behaviour and cycle count
identical (iter/cycle unchanged) and move every EX-side select decode
into registered ID/EX bits.

1. Fully registered binary forward selects (qualifiers folded into ID).
   Replace fwd{1,2}_{ex,wb} with fwd_a_sel[1:0] (rs1 / ALU operand A),
   fwd_b_sel[1:0] (ALU operand B, forced 00 when B is imm/pc-derived),
   fwd_s_sel[1:0] (raw rs2 for branch compare, store data, RVFI):
     00 = ID/EX value, 01 = EX/MEM.alu_result,
     10 = MEM/WB.alu_result, 11 = MEM/WB.read_data.
   Computed in ID with priority EX > WB:
     - ex term: id_ex.reg_write && rd!=0 && rd==rs
                && !(id_ex.is_jalr && jalr_bit1_from_EX)
       (JAL misalign = imm[1] is known at decode: ID clears reg_write for
       a JAL with imm[1]=1; EX still sets is_illegal exactly as today).
     - wb term: ex_mem.reg_write && rd!=0 && rd==rs
                && !mem_misalign(ex_mem); bit0 = ex_mem.ctrl.mem_to_reg.
   These are the only late reg_write clears. div_stall needs no term:
   ID/EX never loads while div_stall is high and the divider already
   latches post-forward operands on div_start (write_data / rs*_val use
   div_rs*_q when is_div). dmem stalls hold ID/EX, EX/MEM and MEM/WB
   data together, so a held select stays exact (lesson r2s1 lockstep
   invariant is unchanged). EX forward muxes become a plain 4:1 case on
   a registered 2-bit select (LUT4 pair + MUX2_LUT5 per bit) with no
   qualifier logic and no WB mux in front: removes 2 levels from every
   path above. EX takes raw MEM/WB alu_result/read_data instead of
   wb_w_data (WB mux stays only for the regfile write port / RVFI).

2. ID-premuxed operand B, no operand-A mux. New ID/EX field op_b:
     R-type: rs2_data; OP-IMM/LOAD/STORE/LUI: imm; AUIPC: pc + imm;
     JAL/JALR: pc + 4  (one small ID adder pc + (is_jump ? 4 : imm)).
   LUI/AUIPC/JAL/JALR use a "pass B" result group, so EX has no
   is_auipc mux on operand A, no ALU_LUI arm, and no post-ALU
   is_jump ? pc+4 mux. Operand A is always forwarded rs1, which also
   feeds branch compare, the jalr/AGU adder and RVFI rs1_rdata.

3. One-hot registered ALU control. Decode in ID and register:
   sub, one-hot groups {add/sub, slt, sltu, and, or, xor, sll, srl/sra,
   pass_b, mul_lo, mul_hi, div}, shift_arith, mul_a_signed,
   mul_b_signed. Share one adder a + (b ^ {32{sub}}) + sub for
   ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU (SLT/SLTU from carry-out and sign/overflow). EX
   output = OR over (grp_i & res_i): ~2 LUT levels instead of 6, and
   the DSP sign bit becomes rs1[31] & registered mul_a_signed. Keep
   alu.sv's divider FSM/handshake unchanged and keep the
   RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS branch bit-identical (MUL/MULH/MULHU = (a+b)^c,
   MULHSU = (a-b)^c, DIV* = quo_q), selected by the same one-hot bits;
   alu_op is kept in ID/EX for the divider latch / ALTOPS constants.

4. One-hot registered branch op. Register br_eq, br_ne, br_lt, br_ge
   (plus br_unsigned) from ID; compute eq by XOR-reduce and lt/ltu from
   one 33-bit carry-chain subtract of the forwarded operands
   ({~unsigned & rs1[31], rs1} - {~unsigned & rs2[31], rs2}); taken =
   (br_eq & eq) | (br_ne & ~eq) | (br_lt & lt) | (br_ge & ~lt), so the
   compare -> redirect cone drops from 6 LUT levels to ~4.

Estimate: path 1 loses the qualifier level, the operand-A mux and ~3-4
result-mux levels (13.7 -> ~9 ns); paths 3-5 lose the WB mux, the
qualifier and ~2 compare/decode levels (13.6 -> ~10.5-11 ns, becoming
the new critical path together with the DSP multiply path). P0 Fmax
~90 MHz, median ~80-85 MHz vs 67.6 -> fitness ~180 (+20%), cycles
unchanged. Area cost: ~96 ID/EX flops (op_b, selects, one-hot bits) and
~100 LUTs, well under budget. After implementation, run `make timing
TARGET=bench`; if the ID-side path (imem data -> decode/regfile ->
op_b / select compare -> ID/EX) becomes worst, drop the ID pc+imm
adder for AUIPC (keep pc in a pass-through and add it in EX) before
anything else.

changes.description: id_ex_t: replace fwd1_ex/fwd1_wb/fwd2_ex/fwd2_wb with fwd_a_sel[1:0], fwd_b_sel[1:0], fwd_s_sel[1:0]; add op_b[31:0] (ID-premuxed operand B) and registered one-hot ALU control (sub, res_add, res_slt, res_sltu, res_and, res_or, res_xor, res_sll, res_sr, res_passb, res_mul_lo, res_mul_hi, res_div, shift_arith, mul_a_signed, mul_b_signed) and one-hot branch bits (br_eq, br_ne, br_lt, br_ge, br_unsigned). Keep alu_op/branch_op for the divider latch, ALTOPS constants and RVFI-neutral uses.

Output 2-bit binary selects (00 ID/EX value, 01 EX/MEM alu_result, 10 MEM/WB alu_result, 11 MEM/WB read_data) for operand A (rs1), operand B (rs2, forced 00 when op_b is imm/pc-derived) and raw rs2; EX priority over WB; x0 never forwards; ex term gated by !(ID/EX is_jalr && jalr_bit1), wb term gated by !mem_misalign(EX/MEM) with bit0 = EX/MEM mem_to_reg.

Compute op_b (R-type rs2_data; imm for OP-IMM/LOAD/STORE/LUI; pc+imm for AUIPC; pc+4 for JAL/JALR); decode and register the one-hot ALU-result, sub, shift, multiplier-sign and branch-op bits; clear reg_write at decode for JAL with imm[1]=1; take new inputs (EX jalr_bit1 + ID/EX is_jalr, EX/MEM mem_to_reg and mem_misalign) for the forward pre-decode; new fields load under the same !stall condition; flush still clears only the existing kill bits.

Optionally emit the one-hot result-group / sub / shift_arith / mul-sign / branch one-hot bits directly (is_illegal default and validated arms unchanged); otherwise derive them in id_stage from alu_op/branch_op.

Forward muxes become plain 4:1 cases on the registered 2-bit selects (no reg_write qualifiers, no WB mux); ALU operand A = forwarded rs1, operand B = forwarded op_b; delete the is_auipc/alu_src operand muxes and the post-ALU is_jump ? pc+4 mux; branch condition from registered one-hot bits with XOR-reduce eq and a 33-bit carry-chain subtract for lt/ltu; export jalr_bit1; divider operand latching, div_stall bubbles, misalign traps, redirect, AGU and RVFI fields (rs1_val/rs2_val = forwarded architectural register values) unchanged.

Replace the 5-bit op case with an AND-OR of one-hot registered group selects; single shared adder a + (b ^ {32{sub}}) + sub feeding ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU; pass_b group for LUI/AUIPC/JAL/JALR; multiplier sign bits from registered controls; divider FSM and handshake unchanged; RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS substitutions kept bit-identical.
Export the combinational mem_misalign bit (computed from registered EX/MEM fields) for the ID-side forward qualifier; no functional change.
Rewire: EX/MEM mem_to_reg + mem_misalign and EX jalr_bit1 into id_stage; raw MEM/WB alu_result and read_data into ex_stage in place of fwd_mem_wb / mem_wb_reg_write.
Drive the new one-hot ALU control interface (the controls ID would decode for each op) and keep every existing M-ext and base-op vector.

Compute op_b (R-type rs2_data; imm for OP-IMM/LOAD/STORE/LUI; pc+imm for AUIPC; pc+4 for JAL/JALR); decode and register the one-hot ALU-result, sub, shift, multiplier-sign and branch-op bits; clear reg_write at decode for JAL with imm[1]=1; take new inputs (EX jalr_bit1 + ID/EX is_jalr, EX/MEM mem_to_reg and mem_misalign) for the forward pre-decode; new fields load under the same !stall condition; flush still clears only the existing kill bits.

Optionally emit the one-hot result-group / sub / shift_arith / mul-sign / branch one-hot bits directly (is_illegal default and validated arms unchanged); otherwise derive them in id_stage from alu_op/branch_op.

Forward muxes become plain 4:1 cases on the registered 2-bit selects (no reg_write qualifiers, no WB mux); ALU operand A = forwarded rs1, operand B = forwarded op_b; delete the is_auipc/alu_src operand muxes and the post-ALU is_jump ? pc+4 mux; branch condition from registered one-hot bits with XOR-reduce eq and a 33-bit carry-chain subtract for lt/ltu; export jalr_bit1; divider operand latching, div_stall bubbles, misalign traps, redirect, AGU and RVFI fields (rs1_val/rs2_val = forwarded architectural register values) unchanged.

Replace the 5-bit op case with an AND-OR of one-hot registered group selects; single shared adder a + (b ^ {32{sub}}) + sub feeding ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU; pass_b group for LUI/AUIPC/JAL/JALR; multiplier sign bits from registered controls; divider FSM and handshake unchanged; RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS substitutions kept bit-identical.
Export the combinational mem_misalign bit (computed from registered EX/MEM fields) for the ID-side forward qualifier; no functional change.
Rewire: EX/MEM mem_to_reg + mem_misalign and EX jalr_bit1 into id_stage; raw MEM/WB alu_result and read_data into ex_stage in place of fwd_mem_wb / mem_wb_reg_write.
Drive the new one-hot ALU control interface (the controls ID would decode for each op) and keep every existing M-ext and base-op vector.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-001-r3s0 (regression, +27.83%): Moving every EX-side select decode into registered ID/EX bits (fully qualified 2-bit forward selects that read raw MEM/WB alu_result/read_data instead of the WB mux, an ID-premuxed operand B with pc+imm/pc+4 so there is no AUIPC mux on A and no is_jump link mux, a one-hot AND-OR ALU result replacing the 6-LUT 19-way binary case, and registered mul sign bits and one-hot branch op bits) lifted the implied Fmax from 67.6 to about 86 MHz at unchanged cycles, beating its +20% estimate, which shows binary-encoded op decode and select qualifiers in EX are the cheapest Fmax on Gowin LUT4; folding the reg_write qualifiers into ID works only if every late reg_write clear (EX JALR target bit 1, EX/MEM mem_misalign) is fed back into the ID select compare; it still lost to a round-3 sibling, most likely r3s1, which used the same one-hot selects but also resolved MEM/WB forwarding in ID, so EX needs only a 2:1 EX/MEM bypass, so after decode is registered the next lever is the width of EX's forward mux.

title: Resolve operands one stage early: ID-stage forwarding network + ID-precomputed pc-relative results, leaving EX a single registered-select EX/MEM bypass
motivation:
Measured on the champion (make timing, place option 0, 72.8 MHz; the median
across placement options is 67.6 MHz). All top-50 setup paths start at a
forwarding control flop and pass through EX's 3:1 operand-forwarding
network:
  path 1 (19.03 ns, 12 cells): EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write (fanout 81) ->
    rs1 fwd LUT -> rs1 fwd LUT (fanout 38) -> alu_a AUIPC mux ->
    mul_a sign-ext LUT -> DSP (3.76 ns) -> six-LUT ALU result mux
    (n764_s13..s0) -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
  paths 2-5 (18.9-19.0 ns): MEM/WB.ctrl.mem_to_reg -> u_wb write-data
    mux -> EX rs2 fwd mux -> six-LUT branch comparator -> redirect ->
    PC mux -> pc_w. The same chain also ends at the ID/EX kill bits
    (via flush_id) and at alu_result.
So about 3 LUT levels plus the high-fanout nets before the ALU/comparator
are pure operand routing: the WB select, the 3:1 forward select, the
EX/MEM reg_write qualifier and the AUIPC pc/rs1 select. The six-LUT
binary-encoded 19-way result mux after it is also overhead. None of this
is arithmetic. Most of it can move one stage earlier, because for the
instruction in ID the MEM-stage producer (I-2) and the WB-stage producer
(I-3) are already known and their values are available in that cycle.
Only the immediately-older producer (I-1, which is in EX while the
consumer is in ID) needs a bypass in EX. The same applies to the
pc-relative values (pc+imm for branch/JAL targets and AUIPC, pc+4 for
links, and imm for LUI). They depend only on ID-stage data, but today
they are computed or selected in EX.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the forwarding topology so that EX sees exactly one
bypass level, and move every EX input that does not depend on I-1 into
the ID stage, registered in ID/EX. Cycle behaviour is unchanged: the
stall, flush, load-use and redirect timing are identical, so iter/cycle
stays the same and all gain comes from Fmax.

1. ID-stage forwarding (new rtl/operand_unit.sv or inside id_stage). For
   the raw instruction in ID, each of rs1 and rs2 becomes a priority mux
   with three inputs:
     (a) MEM-stage producer (the current EX/MEM occupant). Its value is
         mem_val = EX/MEM.ctrl.mem_to_reg ? load_data (mem_stage's
         aligned and extended dmem word, same cycle) : EX/MEM.alu_result.
         It is qualified by EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write && !mem_misalign &&
         rd != 0 && rd == rs.
     (b) regfile read with the existing write-first bypass for the WB
         producer (MEM/WB).
   The resolved values are captured in ID/EX.rs1_val and rs2_val.
   mem_stage exports load_data and mem_misalign for this. Exactness is
   the same argument as r2s1's pre-decode: ID/EX loads only when EX/MEM
   and MEM/WB advance, because stall_id covers every dmem_stall and
   div_stall. For a load, the load-use bubble puts the load in EX/MEM
   while the consumer sits in ID, so (a) captures the load data. A dmem
   stall in that cycle holds ID, so the value is taken only when the bus
   delivers.
2. EX keeps only the EX/MEM -> EX bypass:
   rs = fwd_ex_q ? EX/MEM.alu_result : ID/EX.rs_val. This is one LUT4 per
   bit even if the registered EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write qualifier stays in the
   select (f & r ? x : y is exactly 4 inputs). Preferred variant: fold
   the qualifier into the registered bit. fwd_ex is computed in ID as
   (raw rs == ID/EX.rd && ID/EX.ctrl.reg_write && rd != 0 &&
   !ex_misalign_fault), where ex_misalign_fault is the late EX
   reg_write clear. The div_stall bubble needs no term because ID/EX is
   held during div_stall. Duplicate the fwd_ex flops per operand to cut
   the 81/38-fanout nets. The MEM/WB -> EX path (u_wb mux,
   mem_wb_reg_write, fwd_*_wb) is removed from EX entirely.
3. ID precomputes the pc-relative values and registers them in ID/EX:
     - pc_imm = pc + imm: branch target, JAL target and AUIPC result.
     - pc4 = pc + 4: JAL/JALR link value and non-redirect pc_next.
     - pre_result: the AUIPC, LUI or link value, whichever applies.
   EX's alu_a mux (is_auipc ? pc : rs1) disappears, so the ALU and the
   DSP take rs1 directly. The EX branch_target and jump adders
   disappear, so redirect_target = is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1],0} : pc_imm_q.
4. The operand B immediate is pre-selected in ID (op_b = alu_src ? imm :
   resolved rs2). The EX bypass select for op_b is registered as
   fwd2_ex & !alu_src. rs2_val stays a separate bypassed field for store
   data, the branch compare and RVFI rs2_rdata. Keep the EX-side alu_b
   mux with a registered select only if the ID path turns out longer.
5. One-hot result select. ID decodes registered one-hot class selects:
   add/sub, logic, shift, slt, mul_lo, mul_hi, div, pre. EX forms
   alu_result as an AND-OR of the class results (about 3 LUT levels
   instead of 6). The pre_result term replaces the separate
   is_jump ? pc+4 : alu_result mux. mul_a/mul_b sign bits use registered
   a_signed/b_signed flags from ID. Also pre-decode branch_op into
   registered one-hot eq/ne/lt/ge/ltu/geu bits, so the final
   branch_cond select is a flat AND-OR.
Expected critical paths afterwards (from the measured cell delays):
  - ALU/DSP: one bypass LUT, then the DSP, then 3 LUTs. About 9-10 ns
    of data path, compared with 13.7 ns today.
  - Branch -> PC: the u_wb and 3:1 forward levels are gone. About 11 ns
    of data path, compared with 13.6 ns.
  - The new ID-side paths (imem word -> LUT-RAM regfile -> bypass/fwd
    mux -> ID/EX, and dmem BSRAM -> load align -> mem_val -> fwd mux ->
    ID/EX) should stay under that.
Expected Fmax is about 82-90 MHz (median), against 67.6 MHz today, with
cycles unchanged. That is +20-30% fitness, well above the 4.6% bar.
The implementer should run `make timing`. If the dmem -> ID/EX load path
becomes the worst path, merge the regfile write-first bypass and the MEM
forward into one flat 3:1 mux before cutting anything else.
Correctness notes:
  - RVFI rs1_rdata and rs2_rdata must be the post-EX-bypass values, as
    today. The divider still latches post-bypass operands on div_start.
  - The MEM/WB hold semantics can stay as they are; forwarding no longer
    depends on them.
  - Formal (ALTOPS) must keep the M-op substitutions in the same
    one-hot positions.

title: Fetch-cycle predecode predictor (JAL always, bimodal BHT for branches) with 1-cycle EX XOR-mispredict redirect
motivation:
In the champion (r2s1, 67.6 MHz, 4.49M cycles) IF and ID share one cycle:
the PC register addresses imem and the raw io_imemData word is decoded in
the same cycle into ID/EX. Every taken branch, JAL and JALR resolves in EX
and costs one wrong-path bubble. Taken control transfers are about 12% of
CoreMark instructions. Two earlier predictors showed that removing these
bubbles cuts cycles: the r1s2 BTB saved 6.8% and the r2s2 BHT saved 5.0%,
even with a 2-cycle registered mispredict penalty. Both lost on Fmax, but
not because of the predictor. r1s2 was built on the 5 MHz divider-bound
core. r2s2's worst path was rf->ID->ALU->dmem BSRAM address (24.9 ns), the
AGU wall that r2s1 then removed. r2s2 also put a new kill into EX/MEM.
Since IF and ID are one cycle here, a predecode-based prediction needs no
BTB. The fetched word already holds the branch or JAL offset, so pc+imm
can be computed in the fetch cycle and loaded into the PC the same cycle.
A correctly predicted taken JAL or branch then costs 0 bubbles. That
would give the BTB's IPC without its tag/target RAM or its 32-bit
target compare in EX.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a zero-bubble predictor to the fetch/decode cycle. Keep the existing
combinational EX redirect for mispredicts, so the penalty stays 1 cycle
(the same as a taken branch today). Do not add any new EX/MEM kill.

1. Fetch-cycle predecode (if_stage.sv):
   - is_jal = (instr[6:0] == 7'b1101111).
   - is_br = (instr[6:0] == 7'b1100011) && funct3 is not 2 or 3.
   - Use the B- or J-immediate (pure bit wiring).
   - Add a 30-bit adder: tgt = pc[31:2] + imm[31:2]. For timing it is fine
     to use two parallel adders (B and J) and pick the result by
     instr[3].
   - Predict: pred_taken = !imm[1] && (is_jal || (is_br && bht_ctr[1])).
     !imm[1] prevents predicting a misaligned target. Those instructions
     keep today's EX trap-and-no-redirect behavior.
   - PC mux priority:
     redirect ? redirect_target : stall ? pc : pred_taken ? tgt : pc+1.
     redirect stays the last mux level, so the existing EX->PC path does
     not get deeper. The stall gate covers imem-not-ready,
     load-use, dmem and div stalls. In those cases the same word is
     fetched and predicted again later, so the PC advance and the ID/EX
     capture of pred_taken always happen in the same cycle.
   - Export pred_taken and alt_pc = pred_taken ? pc+4 : tgt through
     if_id_t. alt_pc is the address to go to if the prediction was
     wrong.
2. BHT: 64 x 2-bit counters in LUT-RAM (distributed_ram, like reg_file).
   - Read asynchronously at pc[7:2] from the PC register, so the read
     starts right after the flop.
   - Initialize to weakly-not-taken (01) on reset. Clearing the whole
     array is also acceptable.
   - Carry the 2-bit counter value read at fetch through ID/EX and
     EX/MEM.
   - Update one cycle late from registered EX/MEM fields: valid &&
     ctrl.is_branch, the existing branch_taken, pc[7:2] and the carried
     counter. Write the saturated inc/dec at the next clock edge, gated
     by !stall_ex_mem (a held EX/MEM rewrites the same value, which is
     idempotent anyway). This keeps branch_cond, which comes after the
     forward muxes, off the LUT-RAM write-data/setup path.
   - A stale read during the 1-cycle update lag only affects accuracy,
     never correctness.
3. ID/EX (id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv):
   - Add pred_taken, alt_pc[31:2] and bht_ctr[1:0].
   - pred_taken is a kill bit: clear it on flush along with valid,
     is_branch and is_jump, because a flushed slot's prediction was never
     applied (the PC held or was redirected).
4. EX redirect (ex_stage.sv). Rename today's redirect to "taken":
     taken = (branch_taken || is_jump) && !misalign_fault
     redirect = taken ^ in.pred_taken
     redirect_target = is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1], 1'b0} : {alt_pc, 2'b00}
   - A correctly predicted JAL or branch no longer redirects.
   - A predicted-taken branch that falls through redirects to pc+4.
   - A branch predicted not-taken that is taken redirects to pc+imm.
   - JALR is never predicted, so it redirects exactly as today.
   - When pred_taken && taken, the prediction target is by construction
     the same pc+imm the old EX path computed (same raw word, same imm).
     No target compare is needed.
   - Illegal lookalikes can never be predicted, because predecode checks
     the full opcode and branch funct3.
   - The EX path depth is today's cond -> redirect plus at most one LUT
     (XOR with a flop bit). The branch_target adder drops off the
     redirect path because alt_pc comes from a flop. The misalign trap,
     pc_next and RVFI semantics are unchanged: pc_next still reports the
     architectural next PC.
5. Forwarding and hazard logic: no change. The prediction adds no new
   reg_write clear and does not change which stalls ID/EX and EX/MEM
   share. r2s1's pre-decoded fwd bits stay exact.

Expected effect:
  - Removes the bubble for every JAL and for every correctly predicted
    taken branch.
  - Adds a bubble only for not-taken branches mispredicted as taken.
  - Numbers below come from an ISS trace of the timed CoreMark region
    (-O3, 2K, python reference.py, between the 0x10000100 and 0x10000104
    markers): 2.92M instructions, 529.6K branches (294.4K taken), 49.4K
    JALs, 13.7K JALRs. Today's control bubbles are 294.4K + 49.4K +
    13.7K = 357.5K, 8.0% of the champion's 4.49M cycles.
  - The 64-entry bimodal mispredicts 51.8K branches, so the new bubbles
    are 51.8K + 13.7K = 65.6K. That saves 292K cycles, a 6.5% cycle cut
    and about +7.0% fitness at unchanged Fmax.
  - Alternatives from the same trace:
      - static BTFN: 111.2K misses, 5.2% cycle cut.
      - 256-entry bimodal: 44.3K misses, only 0.17% more saved, not worth
        the deeper LUT-RAM read mux.
      - gshare-256: 55.6K misses, worse.
      - A RAS would recover at most 13.7K cycles (0.3%), not worth the
        extra PC-mux input.
  - The new fetch path is LFSR/imem flop -> opcode check -> 30-bit carry
    chain -> 2 mux levels -> PC D, about 10-13 ns. That is well under
    the 19.0 ns EX->ALU->alu_result wall, so Fmax should stay about
    66-68 MHz.
  - Net fitness gain about +5-7%.

changes.description: Add the fetch-cycle predecode: JAL/branch detection, B/J immediate wiring and the pc[31:2]+imm[31:2] target adder (optionally two parallel adders muxed by instr[3]). Add the 64x2 LUT-RAM bimodal BHT: async read at pc[7:2]; a synchronous write port driven by new bht_we/bht_widx/bht_wdata inputs. Compute pred_taken = !imm[1] && (is_jal || (is_br && ctr[1])). PC mux: redirect > stall > pred_taken ? tgt : pc+1. Export pred_taken, alt_pc (pred ? pc+4 : tgt) and ctr through if_id_t.

title: Cut the three tied EX critical-path families together: late-joining multiplier in the result OR tree, divider negate moved out of the start cycle, and a pre-decoded single-comparator redirect
motivation:
Measured on the champion r3s1 with `make timing TARGET=bench` (place
option 0, 85.4 MHz; median 89.4 MHz). The top 25 setup paths lie
within 0.4 ns of each other (16.63-17.01 ns arrival, 11.6-11.7 ns data
delay). Every one starts at the EX/MEM.alu_result bypass flop, and they
fall into three separate families. Fixing any single family gains
almost nothing, which may be why earlier single-path tweaks left
Fmax stuck near 86-89 MHz. All three must be cut in one change:
  F1 (paths 1,2,7,24 -> alu_result): alu_result[4] -> rs1 bypass LUT
     (0.5) -> 1.67 ns net -> DSP (3.76) -> FOUR LUT levels of the
     one-hot result AND-OR (s8 -> s5 -> s3 -> s, ~3.3 ns incl. routing)
     -> EX/MEM.alu_result. The slowest class result (the DSP) enters
     at the deepest level of the OR tree.
  F2 (path 3 -> u_alu/quo_q): alu_result[8] -> rs1 bypass -> 3.9 ns
     net -> SIX-LUT ripple of the `sa ? 0 - a : a` / `sb ? 0 - b : b`
     start-cycle negate -> quo_q/dvs_q. DIV is almost absent from
     CoreMark's timed region, so this path costs Fmax for nothing.
  F3 (paths 4-6,8-23,25 -> if/pc_w CE and D): alu_result[4] -> rs2
     bypass -> 28-bit comparator carry chain -> n37_s15 -> n37_s17 ->
     n37_s11 -> n37_s4 (fanout 31) -> pc_w_28_s3 (fanout 30) -> pc_w CE.
     That is four LUT levels after the carry chain, spent on the
     6-way br_sel select, AND with is_branch, the misalign_branch
     (taken && imm[1]) suppression and the jump OR, before the PC
     enable.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Cycle behaviour stays identical except for +1 cycle per DIV/REM (negligible
in CoreMark). All the gain comes from Fmax, by removing LUT levels from the
three tied families together.

A. Multiplier joins the result OR tree last (alu.sv). Split `out` into
   two explicitly kept partial ORs:
     fast_or = the AND-OR of ADD, SUB, AND, OR, XOR, SLT, SLTU, SLL, SR,
               DIV (quo_q) and PRE
     mul_or  = (sel[RS_MULLO] & prod[31:0]) | (sel[RS_MULHI] & prod[63:32])
               (one LUT4 per bit)
     out     = fast_or | mul_or
   Put `(* syn_keep = 1 *)` on fast_or and mul_or so Gowin synthesis
   cannot re-collapse them into the 4-deep tree. The DSP output then
   passes through 2 LUT levels instead of 4, about -1.5 to -2 ns on F1.
   Optionally feed the DSP from its own copy of the EX/MEM bypass mux
   (a duplicated registered fwd select, syn_keep), so the 72-fanout
   1.67 ns net is shared less. The ALTOPS mul_lo/mul_hi stand-ins take
   the same mul_or slot.

B. Divider prep cycle (alu.sv). On div_start, latch the raw post-bypass
   a/b plus sa, sb and is_rem, with no arithmetic. Add a PREP state
   (one cycle) that applies quo_q <= sa ? -quo_q : quo_q,
   dvs_q <= sb ? -dvs_q : dvs_q and
   neg_quo_q <= (sa ^ sb) && (dvs_q != 0) from flops. Then run the
   existing 32 iterations and the fix-up cycle (35 cycles instead of 34).
   This removes F2 entirely, since the start-cycle inputs become plain
   flop loads. The ALTOPS branch keeps its start -> fix-up -> done
   handshake (the PREP state can be skipped under ALTOPS, or kept to
   exercise one more stall cycle; both are formally fine).

C. Pre-decoded single-comparator redirect (id_stage.sv, ex_stage.sv,
   core_pkg.sv). Register in ID/EX:
     br_use_lt = funct3[2], br_inv = funct3[0], br_uns = funct3[1]
     br_ok     = is_branch && !imm[1]   (may redirect)
     br_bad    = is_branch &&  imm[1]   (traps if taken)
     jal_ok    = JAL && !imm[1],  jal_bad = JAL && imm[1]
   These are kill bits: flush clears them like is_branch/is_jump.
   In EX, compute one 33-bit signed less-than
   {rs1[31] & ~br_uns, rs1} < {rs2[31] & ~br_uns, rs2} (one carry chain
   instead of separate lt/ltu chains) and eq. Then
   cond = (br_use_lt ? lt : eq) ^ br_inv (a single LUT4), and
     redirect = (br_ok & cond) | jal_ok | (is_jalr & !jalr_bit1)
   (1-2 LUTs). The trap term misalign_fault = (br_bad & cond) | jal_bad |
   (is_jalr & jalr_bit1) now feeds only EX/MEM flops (ctrl_with_trap,
   fwd_ok) and ex_wb_kill (= jal_bad | is_jalr & jalr_bit1), so it is
   off the PC path. In if_stage, keep a syn_keep duplicate of redirect
   for the pc_w enable separate from the one steering the D-mux and
   flush_id, so the fanout-31/30 nets split. This cuts about 2 LUT
   levels (~1.3-1.8 ns) from F3.

Expected: all three families drop by at least 1.3 ns. The next wall is
likely bypass -> adder/shifter -> AND-OR, around 10.3-10.8 ns of data
delay, so median Fmax goes from ~89.4 to ~95-99 MHz (+6-10%) with
CoreMark cycles unchanged. Exactness of the pre-decoded forwards
(LESSONS r2s1/r3s1) holds: no new late reg_write clear is introduced.
ex_wb_kill and fwd_ok keep the same logical value, only computed from
pre-decoded bits.

title: Empty the EX bypass loop: MUL*/DIV* become load-like MEM-stage results, divider operand prep moves off the bypass, redirect becomes the last PC data-mux select
motivation:
Re-timed the champion (r3s1) with `make timing` (place option 0, 85.4 MHz,
constraint 5 ns, clock insertion 5.33 ns). All ~25 failing setup paths
start at the EX/MEM->EX bypass source (EX/MEM.alu_result) and fall into
three families whose data paths are within 0.08 ns of each other
(~11.65 ns):
  A. MUL (paths 1,2,7): alu_result_4 -> rs1 bypass LUT (fanout 21,
     1.67 ns route into the DSP column) -> DSP prod A[4]->DOUT[26]
     (3.76 ns) -> 4-LUT one-hot AND-OR -> EX/MEM.alu_result_26. 17.008 ns.
  B. DIV start (path 3): alu_result_8 -> rs1 bypass LUT (fanout 18,
     3.87 ns route) -> 5 LUTs of `sa ? 0-a : a` -> u_alu/quo_q_15.
     16.980 ns. The divider latches its sign-magnitude operands straight
     off the bypass in the div_start cycle.
  C. Branch -> PC (paths 4-6, 8-15, ~20 endpoints): alu_result_4 -> rs2
     bypass LUT -> 32-cell compare carry chain -> FIVE LUT levels
     (br_sel AND-OR, is_branch/misalign qualify, redirect, redirect|!stall,
     fanout-31/30 duplicate) -> pc_w CE. 16.972 ns.
So removing any single family buys nothing (the other two sit 0.03 ns
behind): the multiplier, the divider prep and the redirect->PC tail must
leave the loop together. MUL/DIV are rare in CoreMark's timed region
(~1-2k MUL, ~0 DIV per iteration vs ~449k cycles/iteration), so turning
them into late (MEM-stage) results costs <0.4% cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the 4-deep IF/ID -> EX -> MEM -> WB pipeline and every stall/flush/
forward timing, but move everything that is not base-ALU or branch out of
the EX->EX recurrence.

1. M-unit results become load-like MEM-stage results.
   - EX: the post-bypass operands are captured at the end of EX into
     dedicated 33-bit sign-extended registers mul_a_q/mul_b_q (a_signed/
     b_signed applied before the flop, loaded when EX/MEM advances) plus
     a registered hi/lo select and a registered `mdu` bit. Plain flops,
     so Gowin can pack them as the DSP input registers.
   - MEM: mdu_res = is_mul_q ? (hi ? prod[63:32] : prod[31:0]) : quo_q;
     nonload = mdu_q ? mdu_res : alu_result (one LUT, in parallel with the
     BSRAM read), fwd_val = mem_to_reg ? load_data : nonload (same 2:1 as
     today), and MEM/WB.alu_result captures `nonload` so WB/RVFI rd_wdata
     are unchanged. quo_q is stable while the DIV sits in MEM (the next
     div_start overwrites it only at the edge where MEM/WB captures it).
   - EX result AND-OR drops RS_MULLO, RS_MULHI and RS_DIV (11 -> 8 live
     terms per bit), so the DSP and quo_q both leave the EX loop.
   - Interlock: ID registers `late_res` = mem_read || is_mul || is_div in
     ID/EX (cleared by the kill-bit flush). hazard_unit's load-use compare
     keys on id_ex_late_res instead of id_ex_mem_read, so a consumer
     directly behind a MUL/DIV takes the existing one-cycle bubble and then
     receives the product via ID's MEM-stage forward (EX/MEM.fwd_ok is
     already reg_write && rd!=0). No new late reg_write clear, so r3s1's
     fwd_ex/fwd_ok exactness argument is unchanged; fwd_ex for a late
     occupant is never consumed because of the interlock.
2. Divider prep off the bypass. div_start only latches the raw post-bypass
   rs1/rs2 (div_rs1_q/div_rs2_q already exist for RVFI). A new one-cycle
   PREP state loads quo_q/dvs_q/neg flags (sign-magnitude negate) from
   those registers; then 32 iterations, fix-up, done (35 cycles, +1).
   ALTOPS path: same PREP state, stand-in formula still applied in fix-up.
3. Short redirect -> PC tail.
   - ID pre-decodes and registers: br_sel gated by is_branch && !imm[1]
     (misaligned-if-taken branches never redirect; a separate registered
     br_trap bit still drives rvfi_trap via branch_taken && imm[1]),
     jal_go = is_jal && !imm[1], and is_jalr. EX then forms
     redirect = |(br_sel & {..!ltu,ltu,!lt,lt,!eq,eq}) | jal_go |
                (is_jalr & !jalr_bit1) -> one LUT level after the compare.
   - if_stage: no clock-enable. pc_w <= redirect ? target[31:2]
     : pc_w + {29'b0, !stall_if}. stall_if feeds only the incrementer carry-in,
     and redirect is the last 2:1 select on the D input, instead of going
     through redirect|!stall into 30 CE pins.
Net: family A and B leave the loop entirely, family C loses ~3 LUT levels
(~1.5-2 ns). The next tier (shifter/adder -> 8-term AND-OR -> EX/MEM,
compare -> PC mux) should be ~10.2-10.8 ns. Expect Fmax 89 -> ~97-100 MHz
with iter/cycle down <0.5%.

No-CE PC: pc_w <= redirect ? target : pc_w + !stall (stall only on the incrementer carry-in, redirect is the final data-mux select).
id_ex_t: late_res, mdu, is_mul, jal_go, br_trap; ex_mem_t: mdu, is_mul.
Rewire hazard_unit to id_ex_w.late_res, connect mul_unit/quo_q into mem_stage.
Move multiply bit-exact vectors to a registered mul_unit harness (check product one cycle after load); account for the +1 PREP cycle in divider vectors; keep base-ALU vectors.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-002-r4s1 (regression, +12.25%): Attacking the same three tied r3s1 path families as sibling r4s0, but by restructuring the pipeline (MUL*/DIV* results moved to MEM behind a load-like `late_res` interlock with DSP input flops, a no-CE PC `pc_w <= redirect ? target : pc_w + !stall_if`, and a registered br_sel with imm[1] misalign folded in) instead of splitting logic, reached about 100 MHz implied (223.50) and met its own 97-100 MHz estimate, but lost to r4s0 (232.94, 104.6 MHz), which used the same flop-only DIV start plus prep cycle but kept MUL in EX behind a `(* syn_keep *)` fast_or/mul_or late-join split with a duplicated redirect CE; r4s0's worst path is already the base-ALU loop both designs share (alu_result -> alu_result, 5 cells), so r4s1's ~4% deficit is mostly Fmax (its MUL-consumer bubbles were estimated at <0.4% of cycles) and likely comes from paths the restructure added, such as the `mdu_q ? mdu_res : alu_result` mux on the MEM->ID forward value or stall_if driving the 30-bit PC incrementer carry chain; so when a syn_keep late-join split can take a slow unit off the EX bypass loop, moving that unit to a later pipeline stage does not pay for its extra muxes and interlock.

title: PC-indexed 32-entry LUT-RAM BTB; EX checks prediction via pre-swapped branch selects and a flop-only target compare, keeping redirect depth
motivation:
On the r3s1 champion (89.4 MHz, 4.49M cycles) IF and ID share one cycle
and EX redirects, so every taken branch / JAL / JALR costs exactly one
bubble. The ISS trace in r1s2 measured 12.2% of retired instructions as
taken transfers (294k taken branches, 49k JAL, 14k JALR per 2.92M) and
sized a direct-mapped BTB with allocate-on-taken 2-bit counters:
32 entries save 0.103 CPI, 64 save 0.105, RAS adds nothing. r1s2's real
cycle cut was 6.8% (4.49M -> 4.19M), r3s2's 6.5%.
The three earlier predictors lost it on Fmax, not on IPC: r1s2 sat on a
5 MHz divider core, r2s2 added an EX/MEM kill and a fetch-predecode
adder, and r3s2 put imem data -> opcode -> 30-bit pc+imm adder -> PC mux
in the fetch cycle and ended ~6% below its parent. r3s2's worst path was
still the EX ALU loop, so its loss was mostly extra logic and placement
noise. LESSONS asks for a registered, PC-indexed target (BTB-style) and
no new depth on EX->redirect->PC. This design does both: the only new
fetch path starts at the PC flop, and every new EX term is
flop-early except the existing branch compare.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. BTB (new rtl/btb.sv): 32 entries, direct-mapped, index pc[6:2], partial
   tag pc[14:7] (8 bits), target pc[19:2] (18 bits, all legal code is below
   0x00100000), 2-bit counter. Stored as distributed LUT-RAM (28 bits x 32,
   two RAM16 banks), asynchronous read addressed by the PC flop, one
   synchronous write port. No valid bits and no reset: arbitrary or zero
   contents only cost a mispredict, because EX checks every prediction.
   Gowin initializes LUT-RAM to 0 (ctr=0, not taken). For Verilator, add
   an `initial` zero fill if needed.
   hit = (tag == pc[14:7]); pt = hit && ctr[1] && !suppress_q.
   pred_npc = {pc[31:20], tgt}.
2. IF PC mux: redirect ? redirect_target : stall ? pc : pt ? pred_npc :
   pc+1. Redirect stays the last level. The new path is PC flop -> LUT-RAM
   -> 8-bit tag compare -> 30-bit mux, about 6-7 ns against an 11.2 ns
   period, and it does not touch imem data. The PC advance and the ID/EX
   capture happen in the same cycle (both need no stall and no redirect),
   so the pt latched into ID/EX is always the prediction that steered the
   PC.
3. ID registers into ID/EX (pt is a kill bit, cleared on flush):
     pt, btb_hit, btb_ctr[1:0], pred_tgt[19:2]
     br_sel_x = pt ? swap(br_sel) : br_sel  (eq<->ne, lt<->ge, ltu<->geu)
     alt_pc   = pt ? pc4 : pc_imm   (same depth as the existing pre_result
                                     mux after the pc_imm adder)
     br_en    = is_branch && !imm[1]
     jal_redir = is_jal && !pt && !imm[1]
   br_sel_x makes EX's existing one-hot AND-OR produce "outcome !=
   prediction" directly, with no XOR level (r3s2's mistake).
4. EX, normal case:
     redirect = bad_pt || (br_en && cond_x) || jal_redir
                || (is_jalr && !jalr_bit1)
     redirect_target = (is_jalr && !bad_pt) ? jalr_sum
                       : (bad_pt ? pc : alt_pc)
   The target mux keeps today's shape: one early select and late data only
   on jalr_sum. The bad_pt/alt_pc pre-mux is early.
   A correctly predicted taken branch or JAL now costs 0 bubbles. A
   predicted-taken branch that falls through redirects to pc4 (1 bubble,
   the same as a taken branch today).
5. EX, bad prediction (aliasing, JALR/non-control hit, misaligned target,
   or symbolic formal streams):
     tgt_ok = ({pc[31:20], pred_tgt} == pc_imm[31:2]), computed from
              ID/EX flops only (3 LUT levels, parallel to the fwd-mux +
              carry-chain compare)
     bad_pt = valid && pt && !((is_branch || is_jal) && !imm[1] && tgt_ok)
   Early. It replays the instruction:
     - redirect to its own pc;
     - EX/MEM takes a bubble (valid, reg_write, mem_read/write and fwd_ok
       cleared, as for the div bubble);
     - OR bad_pt into ex_wb_kill. The ID slot is always flushed on the
       same cycle, but this keeps the r3s1 forward-qualifier rule.
     - gate div_stall and div_start with !bad_pt;
     - set IF suppress_q. It forces pt=0 until the PC next advances
       without a redirect, so the refetched instruction goes through
       unpredicted. This guarantees liveness.
   CoreMark code is static and fits in the 8-bit tag reach (32 KB), so
   replays essentially never happen at run time. They exist only for
   correctness.
6. Training (fed only by flops): write from EX/MEM when valid && (is_branch
   || JAL) && !trap. Add the fetched btb_hit/btb_ctr to EX/MEM, and set
   EX/MEM.branch_taken = is_branch && (cond_x ^ pt), a late XOR that only
   feeds a flop.
     - taken: write {tag, pc_imm[19:2], hit ? sat_inc(ctr) : 2'b10}.
     - JAL: counter 2'b11.
     - not-taken hit: sat_dec(ctr).
     - JALR is never trained.
   EX/MEM never holds a branch across a dmem stall, so each branch trains
   once.
RVFI pc_next stays the architectural next PC. It is RVFI-only and pruned
in synthesis. The misaligned-branch trap uses the actual taken bit, as
today.
Expected: ~6.5% fewer cycles (r1s2/r3s2 measured 6.5-6.8%). Fmax should
stay within ~2%: the worst path (the EX ALU loop) is untouched and the
redirect depth is unchanged. Added cost is about 150 LUT, 14 LUT-RAM
blocks and ~90 FF.

lesson: - 2026-09-30 hyp-20260930-003-r4s2 (regression, +8.36%): A 32-entry PC-indexed LUT-RAM BTB (8-bit partial tag, no valid bits, async read from the PC flop, trained only from EX/MEM flops) whose EX check adds no depth to EX->redirect->PC (br_sel pre-swapped in ID when predicted taken so the existing AND-OR yields "outcome != prediction", an ID-premuxed alt_pc = pt ? pc4 : pc_imm, and a flop-only tgt_ok compare whose bad_pt replays the instruction with the next prediction suppressed) scored 215.76 vs r3s1's 199.11, so if the ~6.5% cycle cut measured by r1s2/r3s2 held, the implied Fmax stayed near 90 MHz and this is the first predictor here to keep its whole IPC gain; it lost only to sibling r4s0 (232.94, 104.6 MHz), whose EX path cuts are orthogonal, so port it onto r4s0 by folding pt into that design's registered branch `inv` bit (inv ^ pt) instead of swapping br_sel, and re-time the PC flop->LUT-RAM->tag compare->PC mux path against r4s0's ~9.6 ns period rather than r3s1's 11.2 ns.

title: Cut all five tied ~10.1 ns families of r4s0: MEM-stage regfile write (no write-first compare), 2-level result OR, bypass-free branch equality, DSP-local bypass copy
motivation:
Measured on the champion r4s0 with `make timing TARGET=bench`
(place option 0: 98.7 MHz; median 104.6). The top paths all sit at
15.39-15.42 ns arrival (~10.1 ns data delay) and fall into five
independent families. The r4s0 lesson says a single-family fix moves
Fmax by almost nothing, so this cuts all five in one change:
 F1 DSP (path 1): EX/MEM.alu_result[8] -> 1.40 ns net -> alu_b bypass
    LUT -> 1.67 ns net (fanout 72) -> DSP B (3.78) -> mul_or -> 1.15 ns
    net -> alu_result. Mostly routing: the shared bypass mux sits far
    from the DSP.
 F2 adder (path 2): alu_b bypass -> 2.05 ns net -> sub_res carry chain ->
    FOUR fast_or LUT levels (s11 -> s7 -> s3 -> s1) -> out LUT. The
    10-term one-hot OR (ADD, SUB, AND, OR, XOR, SLT, SLTU, SLL, SR, DIV,
    PRE) is still 4 levels deep, plus the mul_or join.
 F3 regfile (path 3): raw imem word -> 4-level `w_en && w_addr == rs2`
    write-first compare in reg_file -> fanout-32 select (2.68 ns net) ->
    2-LUT rs2_res forward mux -> 1.55 ns net -> ID/EX.rs2_val. The
    write-first compare is in series with the ID forwarding mux.
 F4 SLT (path 4): alu_b[1] bypass (fanout 77, 2.99 ns net) -> lt compare
    -> SIX LUT levels of fast_or[0] -> out[0]. SLT/SLTU enter at the
    bottom of bit 0's OR tree.
 F5 redirect (paths 5, 18, 21-25): alu_result[3] -> rs1 bypass LUT
    (fanout 19, 1.25 ns net) -> SEVEN LUTs (32-bit eq tree + cond +
    redirect) -> if/n6_s0 (fanout 30) -> pc_w CE/D.

    (fanout 19, 1.25 ns net) -> SEVEN LUTs (32-bit eq tree + cond +
